newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slipped in Wednesday morning trade, continuing their consolidation ahead of another expected move upwards, analysts said.

"From a technical point of view the market is overbought and needs a small correction. The market is still in an uptrend but needs to correct," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng index was down 19.08 points at 12,087.68. Turnover was HK$1.42 billion after the first hour of trade.
Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities, said futures were lending support to the market. October Hang Seng futures were down 30 points to 12,105.
"They are trading at around cash and not at a discount which is encouraging. They are lending support to the consolidation."
"We have a fairly healthy consolidation," Remington added.
Tam said the Hang Seng index could retest 11,900 points before moving higher again.

"Most of the effect of steady U.S. rates is already reflected in the Hong Kong market so from now on the Hong Kong market will depend on local economic fundamentals - earnings and the property market," he said.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank bounced HK$0.75 to HK$85.00 after falling HK$1.75 on Tuesday. However, HSBC Holdings slipped HK$0.50 to HK$145.50.

Property shares were mixed with Sun Hung Kai Properties up HK$0.50 to HK$85.00 and Hang Lung Development up HK$0.05 to HK$15.30 but Henderson Land down HK$0.25 to HK$68.00 and New World Development off HK$0.20 to HK$40.50.
Trading in shares of Shougang Concord International and China Strategic was suspended at the companies' request. Shougang Concord closed at HK$1.19 on Tuesday and China Strategic at HK$2.375.
